festivals: Kali Puja (October-November; the major annual attraction, organized by a dedicated puja committee and drawing hundreds across faiths)

history.dynasty: None (folk/legendary origin - 18th century, Sanyasi-Fakir rebellion era)
history.period: Believed founded in the 18th century; gutted by fire in 2018; meticulously restored and unveiled September 2025
history.summary: The Kali temple near Gosala (Goshala) More, Jalpaiguri town, dedicated to Goddess Kali and named for Devi Chaudhurani, the legendary 'bandit queen' of Bengal folklore (subject of Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's 1884 novel). Legend holds she founded it in the 18th century with her associate Bhavani Pathak; as the tale goes, she looted the rich and distributed to the poor regardless of caste, and people of all communities still attend the Kali Puja here. The temple was tragically gutted by fire in 2018 and has been meticulously restored - unveiled in September 2025 by West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee with new murals depicting the exploits of Devi Chaudhurani and Bhavani Pathak. The reopening coincided with the Bengali film 'Devi Chowdhurani: Bandit Queen of Bengal'. No reliable image of the temple itself could be found after several searches - media left empty. The imimg heritage-tourism PDF confirms the legend (Debi Chaudhurani's Kali Temple near Gosala More, ~3 km from Kadamtala More).

name: Debi Chaudhurani Mandir
town_description: Jalpaiguri is the district headquarter town of North Bengal on the Teesta river, about 40 km southeast of Siliguri. A historic colonial-era town, it serves as the gateway to the Dooars and Bhutan foothills, with local landmarks like Jogomaya Kalibari, the Kalu Saheb mazar, and the Dechen Choiling monastery.

travel.railway: Jalpaiguri Road station in town; New Jalpaiguri (NJP) - about 40 km.
travel.road: Near Gosala More, about 3 km from Kadamtala More, Jalpaiguri town; on NH-27 corridor.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Kali Puja (Oct-Nov) is the grandest but most crowded.
